source.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
source.authors: Jian-Hui Chen; Yu-Zhang Luo; Liang-Ming Pan

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses data deletion and augmentation interventions, then measures induction-head and ICL outcomes. This is a different causal method from the original mechanistic analyses, aimed at related formation and functional-link claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on induction-head scores, ICL scores, and a synthetic copy-task logit contribution. It also reports interventions on previous-token heads, but does not test whether those heads compose with induction heads; those results are not included as rows. OLMo results are qualitative high-influence-sample examples, not tests of induction behaviour. The paper cites other studies' findings, which are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study retrains Pythia-14M to 160M from scratch with targeted and random deletion or augmentation of training data. It measures induction-head prefix-matching scores and the Olsson et al. ICL score. This is a different, causal method aimed at whether and when induction heads form (V5) and how they couple to ICL (V2, V3). The baseline trajectories also show abrupt formation in four Pythia sizes (V2, V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is largely correct. Add that the authors claim direct causal evidence that induction heads are a foundational mechanism for ICL, while acknowledging possible latent confounders. They also report that synthetic data derived from the 14M model accelerates induction-head formation across sizes up to 160M, more so than 160M-derived data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses induction prefix-matching and the Olsson et al. ICL score, but adds influence-function attribution and counterfactual training-data deletion/augmentation rather than directly reproducing the original circuit analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome varies with targeted versus random samples, deletion versus augmentation, model size, natural versus synthetic data, synthetic data source, insertion quantity and schedule, and the choice of full-head versus QK-only probe. The paper reports that dispersed insertion outperforms concentrated insertion for natural data, while synthetic-data insertion shows scale-dependent results.

fits_no_version.finding: Targeted deletion and augmentation of MDA-selected data likewise delay or accelerate previous-token head emergence (Figure 2, lower panels).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Previous-token head formation in pre-trained LMs depends on specific training data.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia-160M, interventions cause one induction head to lose 0.26 in score while other heads compensate. In 14M, head identities stay stable (Appendix F.2, Figure 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In larger models, induction behaviour is redistributed across redundant heads rather than fixed to one head.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Key intervention trajectories in Figures 2, 4d, 5 and 11 are reported as plots, with limited exact numerical values and uncertainty estimates in the text. Causal retraining tests cover Pythia models only up to 160M; OLMo-2-1B and OLMo-2-7B receive qualitative attribution analysis rather than formation interventions. The authors note possible latent confounders in the induction–ICL link and limitations of unit-localized attribution for indirect effects.
record.rows_left_out: No induction-behaviour result within the 60-row limit was omitted. Previous-token-head intervention results were excluded because they do not establish composition with induction heads. Qualitative OLMo samples, SAE examples, MDA ranking-stability statistics, and broad-capability checks were not included because they do not measure the claim's induction or ICL outcomes.

untested.parts: Not tested. There are no attention-only models and no test of composition with a previous-token head; the authors explicitly leave the PT-head-to-induction-head path to future work.
No loss-curve bump is reported. Simultaneity of spontaneous ICL gain with formation in baseline runs is not shown.
Large transformers are not tested. The fraction of ICL carried by induction heads is not quantified.
Only the Pythia family is tested causally; OLMo is qualitative. Other architectures, modalities and independent training seeds for formation are not tested.
Not tested; there is no comparison with other few-shot mechanisms.
Not tested; sub-steps of formation are not examined.

missing.what: Under both augmentation and deletion, models eventually converge to comparable saturation induction scores.
Cross-stage replacement: high-influence samples from early, mid or late steps all beat random replacement by more than 3 standard errors.
An n-gram-matched controlled random augmentation is weaker than MDA augmentation, and a QK-only probe performs worse.
Insertion-quantity and schedule ablation: synthetic data beats natural data for N≤50k and natural beats synthetic at N=100k; dispersed insertion beats concentrated for natural data.
Samples chosen via one induction head transfer to other induction heads but not to non-induction heads.

record.verdict_notes: Pythia models are full transformers with MLPs, not attention-only, so no row bears on V1. All causal evidence covers models of 160M parameters or fewer. Most intervention results are figure-only, without numbers in the text. The model behind Figure 5 (ICL) is not identified.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures induction/copy-target behaviour, but does not directly test whether an induction head forms by composing with an earlier previous-token head.

The study reports abrupt induction-score increases and concurrent intervention-related ICL shifts, but does not report a training-loss bump or establish that spontaneous ICL gain and induction-head formation occur at precisely the same training step.
The study tests ICL-score changes in its Pythia experiments, but does not quantify what fraction of ICL is carried by induction heads, test broad few-shot tasks, or causally test large transformers.

Formation interventions cover four sizes within Pythia; other model families, architectures, modalities, and independent training runs are not tested for induction behaviour. OLMo is analyzed qualitatively only.
The study tests selected data deletion and augmentation conditions; it does not comprehensively vary training-data properties or training setups.
The study does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.
The study does not test whether induction-head formation comprises multiple distinct sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

statements.correction: Figure 5 and Section 5.4: deletion suppresses induction-head formation and degrades ICL; augmentation enhances induction heads and improves ICL. No baseline onset-time ratio or loss bump is reported.
statements.problem: The cited rows establish concurrent responses to training-data interventions, rather than independently establishing coincident onset in unmodified baseline pretraining.

statements.correction: Table 4: analysis windows 1000–1999 for 14M and 0–1199 for 31M. Appendix I.1: dramatic Pythia-14M phase transition between steps 1200 and 2000.
statements.problem: The claim that timing evidence is exclusively graphical overlooks an explicitly stated transition interval; the listed windows are attribution-analysis windows.

statements.correction: Section 5.4: WikiText-2 ICL score L500 − mean(L0:50); intervention-related induction and ICL coupling; possible latent confounders. No total-ICL fraction or large-model causal validation. Figure 5 model labels are garbled. Code availability unresolved.
statements.problem: The coupling description is supported, but it cannot support V3's large-transformer majority claim. Code unavailability is not established by the extracted text.

statements.correction: Data interventions change induction timing and loss-based ICL; majority mediation in large transformers remains untested. Code availability unresolved.
statements.problem: The experimental summary is supported, but listing V3 support exceeds the tested scope. The extracted text does not establish that code is unavailable.
